sections.text: You handled the opening cleanly against the Philidor Defense, gaining space and developing actively. With 5.Bb3 you created a pin against f7, and after castling queenside you looked set to mount an attack along the open g-file. However, 13.Rg2 slowed your momentum, maintaining a pin along the g-file but allowing Black's queen into the game with 13...Qf6.

The game shifted sharply when you grabbed the f4-pawn. 16.Rxf4 ran into 16...Bg5, forcing an exchange of major pieces after 17.Rxf6 Bxd2+ 18.Kxd2 Nxf6. You emerged a pawn down into an endgame where Black held the initiative.

The endgame remained chaotic. You pushed 23.f4 and 24.f5, but Black pushed forward on the queenside. After 26...Rad8, you had a chance to stabilize, but 27.Kc1 left your knight vulnerable to 27...h4. Black trapped the knight with 28...hxg3, leaving you down a piece, and Black converted the extra material comfortably.

sections.text: You chose an early kingside expansion and central occupation in the opening, leading to an open position once pawns were traded with 14.exd5 exd5. When White retreated with 16.Bd2, you missed a chance to blow open the center immediately, but White soon overreached with an unsound sacrifice on your kingside.
